# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐]

I am Deaf: I can see the bomb, I can gesture to Mute, and both Mute and Blind can hear me speak — but I can never hear anyone back, so anything I want known I must send now, complete. What just reached me: Blind waved, Mute waved, and then Mute signed a run of five hand shapes that reads like a counting scale — one, two, three, four, five — almost certainly Mute establishing a numeric gesture code with me, since Mute is the only one who sees my gestures and gestures are our only fast private channel. The most useful thing I own right now is the bomb's appearance, and nobody but me has it. Mute needs it for the manual, Blind needs it to correlate touch with position, and both need to hold off on any action until Mute has checked the rules. So this turn I will speak the full visual state to both of them at once, confirm Mute's counting code by echoing it back as a gesture, ask Blind to describe touch but not act, and promise to re-report the display and light each round in case they change.

```
speak(text="Hello Mute, hello Blind, this is Deaf. I saw both waves, and Mute I saw your five hand signs: I read them as counting, one two three four five. Confirmed, I will use that as our number code in gestures back to you. Here is everything I see on the bomb. The display shows the number 6. The indicator light is yellow. There are five wires, numbered 1 to 5, with the number printed beside each: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is white, wire 3 is purple, wire 4 is green, wire 5 is yellow. That is all I can find, no other markings. Mute: please read the manual for what a display, a light and five wires mean together, and tell Blind exactly what to do, step by step. Blind: please tell Mute everything you can feel, how many wires, their order, and anything you can read by touch, but do not cut, pull or press anything until Mute gives you explicit instructions. I will report the display and the light again every round in case they change.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Blind signed 👍 🤝 — thumbs up and handshake: "understood, agreed." Blind heard my full report, so that's confirmation the voice channel works and Blind is holding off until Mute instructs. Mute signed 🖐 — a five — most likely confirming my echo of the counting code, or confirming "five wires received." Either way, the two-way gesture channel with Mute is now proven working: Mute sees my signs, I see Mute's.

The bomb itself is unchanged: display still 6, light still yellow, same five wires. My remaining value is (a) confirming receipt so nobody wastes turns re-sending, (b) locking in a small shared code with Mute for fast status, and (c) promising instant re-reports whenever Blind completes an action, since Mute can't see the result and I can't hear it — Blind waving plus my spoken report closes that loop.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Blind: your thumbs up and handshake read as understood and agreed, same to you, stay put until Mute speaks. Mute: I received your five, counting code confirmed both ways. Status report: nothing has changed. Display still shows 6, light still yellow, wires one blue, two white, three purple, four green, five yellow. Mute, let's add four more gesture meanings: I will sign thumbs up for confirmed, thumbs down for no, clapping hands for the display or light just changed, and raised open hand for stop everything. When you have finished instructing Blind by voice, sign me a thumbs up so I know it is done. Blind: after you complete any action, wave so I see it, and I will immediately report the new display and light by voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👏", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👌 👍]

Reading this round: Blind sent 👍 — acknowledged, still waiting. Mute sent 👎 👌 👍 — with my proposed codes that's "no, four, confirmed," and with the counting scale 👌 is also "four." That's genuinely ambiguous: it could mean "not done yet / okay / yes," or something about four, or a rejection of part of my code. I can't resolve it this round, and Mute can't hear me ask and answer within one turn — so the right move is to stop ambiguity at the source: publish a complete, unambiguous code now, in one speech, so every future message from Mute arrives as structured instructions instead of vibes.

The critical structural fact I have to make explicit: Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures — so **nobody can instruct Blind except through me**. Mute signs me, I speak it to Blind. That makes my relay the whole pipeline, and it's why this codebook matters more than anything else I do.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Status report first: nothing has changed. Display still 6, light still yellow, wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Extra detail for the manual: the display is a digital readout showing the digit 6, the yellow light sits above the wires, and there are no words, labels or other markings printed anywhere on the bomb. Mute: your last three signs, thumbs down, ok, thumbs up, were ambiguous, so let us fix one exact code, right now, and use only this from now on. Numbers: one is pointing up, two is victory fingers, three is horn fingers, four is the ok ring, five is open hand. Colors: blue is call-me hand, white is crossed fingers, purple is rock horns, green is finger snap, yellow is spock hand. Actions: cut is fist, pull is pointing up, press is pointing down, hold is pinched fingers. Signals: question or I-need-info is small pinch, yes or confirmed is thumbs up, no or wrong is thumbs down, stop everything is raised open hand, display or light just changed is clapping. You send signs left to right. Fist then three means cut wire three. Fist then yellow means cut the yellow wire. If you need anything from me, send the small pinch and I will answer by voice, which you can hear. And if your thumbs down, ok, thumbs up simply meant code accepted, send one thumbs up next turn. Blind: here is the key fact, Mute cannot speak and you cannot see Mute's signs, so every instruction must pass through me. From now on, act only when you hear me say the words: Mute instructs, followed by the exact step. Repeat the step back to Mute out loud so Mute can correct me if my relay is wrong. Until then, hands off everything. Mute: send thumbs up once you have read the manual section covering this display, light and wires.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 👌 ✊ 🫰 🤏 🙌]

Decoding Mute's line with our codebook: 👍 = "code accepted" (answering my request), then ✊ 👌 = "cut four," then ✊ 🫰 = "cut green" — and wire 4 **is** the green wire, so Mute has doubly-encoded one instruction: cut wire 4, green. That redundancy is a good sign the manual pointed at that specific wire. But then comes 🤏 and 🙌 — and here I have to flag my own error: in my codebook I clumsily assigned 🤏 to *both* "hold" (action) and "small pinch" (question), and 🙌 is undefined entirely. So the tail of the message reads either "cut 4/green… I have a question…" or "cut 4/green… HOLD, STOP — not yet." Reading it as "instruction on file, but hold" is the only safe interpretation: if Mute had wanted the cut immediately, a trailing stop would be nonsense, while a pending question explains the hold perfectly. And the display still reads a constant 6 across four turns — it is not counting down — so one round of caution costs nothing.

My move: report full status again (answering every plausible question Mute might have), state my reading, give Mute a one-sign way to say "go" next round, patch the codebook bug, and hold Blind's hands down until the words "Mute instructs: go" come out of my mouth.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Mute, here is how I read your signs: code accepted; instruction is cut wire 4, which is the green wire; then hold, stop, not yet. If that is right, sign one thumbs up next turn. If you actually want Blind to cut wire 4 immediately, sign fist then the ok ring next turn and I will relay it as go. Meanwhile, here are answers to anything you might need: the display still shows a constant 6, it has not changed in four turns, so it is not a countdown. The yellow light is steady, not blinking. There are exactly five wires, in printed order 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Nothing on the bomb has changed since the start. There are no words, numbers, labels, ports or serial markings anywhere except the display and the printed wire numbers. Also, a code fix, my fault: the pinched fingers sign means hold, only hold. From now on, a wave means I have a question, and raised double hands means wait, not yet. Blind: do not touch anything. The instruction cut wire 4 green is on file but on hold. You will act only when you hear me say the exact words: Mute instructs, go. When you do cut, say out loud which wire you are cutting as you cut it, then wave so I can check the display and light and report the result. Mute, Blind: can you both confirm you hear this by signing or gesturing a thumbs up next turn.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤏"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 👌]

Mute's line is the release I asked for. Last turn I told Mute: "if my reading is right, sign one thumbs up; if you want the cut immediately, sign fist then ok-ring." Mute sent **both** — thumbs up, then fist + ok-ring. That's not contradiction, it's sequence: "yes, you read me correctly, and now: cut 4." The hold signs (🤏 🙌) are gone, and Mute heard my complete status report last round — display frozen at 6, light steady, no hidden markings — which was presumably what the hold was waiting on. Three encodings across two turns have now all pointed at the same target: wire 4, green. That's as confirmed as this channel gets. It's time to use the exact phrase I promised Blind, and — critically — Blind cannot see the printed wire numbers, so I must give a touch-navigable route to wire 4 before saying go, including the mirror-flip danger: counted from the wrong end, the fourth wire is wire 2, white. I'll describe the row's geography, mark wire 4's landmarks (second from one end, adjacent to yellow-5, far from blue-1), and have Blind announce before cutting so Mute hears the relay verbatim.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Status first: display still 6, yellow light still steady, five wires unchanged. Now the instruction. Mute instructs: go. Cut wire 4, the green wire. Blind, listen carefully before you act. The five wires run in a single row. From my view, left to right, they are: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Wire 4 green is the fourth counting from the blue end, and it is second from the opposite end, directly beside the last wire in the row, which is 5 yellow. Warning: if you count from the wrong end, the fourth wire is 2 white instead, so fix your reference end before you touch anything. If you can feel any ridges, numbers or texture differences under your fingers, use them to find the green one's position. When your hand is on your chosen wire, say out loud: cutting wire 4, green. Then cut it fully in one motion. Afterward, wave, and I will immediately report the display and light. Mute: I am relaying your go to Blind verbatim this turn, and Blind will repeat the step aloud so you can catch any error. The cut should happen before my next report. As soon as you see or hear the result, send your next instruction in the same code, fist plus a number or fist plus a color. If anything changes on the bomb before Blind cuts, I will say stop immediately. Blind: go now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[yellow] 4:[CUT] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The cut was correct — and the bomb immediately reconfigured. This is the crucial catch: it's not just that green wire 4 is gone. The remaining wires have **recolored and reshuffled**: what was 1 blue 2 white 3 purple 5 yellow is now 1 white 2 purple 3 yellow 5 blue. Every old color-to-position mapping is dead, and the light has changed from yellow to white — that's almost certainly a new module state the manual needs to see. The display alone is unchanged at 6. Mute can't see any of this and my voice is the only pipeline, so this report is the whole game right now. I'll spell out the recoloring explicitly so Mute doesn't evaluate the bomb against stale data, confirm to Blind that the cut was correct and hands stay off, and ping Mute with my "changed" sign as redundant alarm.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Blind: the cut was correct, the system confirmed it, well done, hands off everything now until the next instruction. Everyone, important: the bomb has changed. The light is no longer yellow, it is now white. The display still shows 6, unchanged. And listen carefully: the wires have recolored. The colors did not stay in place after the cut. The new state, printed numbers and all: wire 1 is now white, wire 2 is now purple, wire 3 is now yellow, wire 4 is cut, wire 5 is now blue. So the old mapping is void, blue is now the last wire on the row, at position 5. Cut wire 4 is still visibly cut. That is everything I can see, no other markings. Mute: here is the new full picture for the manual, white light, display 6, four intact wires in order white, purple, yellow, then blue after the cut one. Send your next instruction in the code, fist plus number or fist plus color, with holds if needed. Blind: same drill as before, you act only when you hear me say the words Mute instructs, go, then announce the wire aloud before cutting, then wave.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[yellow] 4:[CUT] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 🤟 ✊ 🖖]

Mute's line decodes clean, no holds this time: 👍 confirms my last report received, then ✊ 🤟 = "cut three," then ✊ 🖖 = "cut yellow" — and the new wire 3 **is** yellow, so both encodings converge on the same target again. Mute heard my full recolor report and this instruction is based on the new state, not the old. With no hold signs appended, this is a straight go. Best of all, wire 3 is the exact middle of the five-wire row — third from either end — so the mirror-flip trap from last time doesn't exist here, and Blind has a superb tactile anchor: the severed wire. I'll relay with full route description and both safety drills.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Brief status: no change, display 6, white light steady, wires as I reported. Now the instruction. Mute instructs: go. Cut wire 3, which is now the yellow wire. Blind, here is your route. Good news: this one is flip-proof. Wire 3 is the exact middle of the five-wire row, the third wire counting from either end, so it does not matter which end you start from. Better anchor still: you cut wire 4 last turn, so you can feel the severed wire. Wire 3 is the intact wire directly beside the cut one, on the side away from the blue wire, between the cut wire and a purple wire. Feel for the cut stub, step one wire over on the far side from blue, and that is your target. Before you cut, say out loud: cutting wire 3, yellow. Then cut it fully in one motion. Afterward wave, and I will report the new display and light immediately, because last time the bomb changed its whole wiring after a correct cut. Mute: relaying your go verbatim now, Blind will announce the step aloud before cutting so you can catch any relay error. Same as before, if anything on the bomb changes before the cut, I will say stop out loud. Blind: go now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Second correct cut confirmed, and the reshuffle struck again — plus two new developments for the manual: the **display changed** for the first time (6 → 9) and the light moved again (white → green). The remaining three intact wires have recolored and re-sorted once more: purple now leads at position 1, blue sits at 2, white trails at 5, and the two severed wires are now adjacent in the middle of the row. If the display increments per correct cut (6 → 9, maybe counting down by threes or just tracking progress), Mute may be able to infer the module's rule — but that's Mute's call, not mine. My job is a fast, exact report so no one evaluates against stale state.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Blind: cut two was correct, system confirmed it, hands off until the next go. Everyone, the bomb changed again, and this time more than the wires. Report of the full new state. The display has changed for the first time: it no longer shows 6, it now shows 9. The light is no longer white, it is now green, steady. The wires have recolored and reshuffled again. New state: wire 1 is purple, wire 2 is blue, wires 3 and 4 are both cut, wire 5 is white. So the two cut wires are now next to each other in the middle of the row, and the three intact wires are purple first, blue second, white last. Three intact wires remain. Mute, one observation for the manual, judge it yourself: after the first correct cut the display held at 6, but after this second cut it now reads 9. If that means the display ticks with each correct cut, it may be tracking progress, but I do not know the rule, the light has gone yellow, then white, then green. Send the next instruction in the usual code, with holds if you need more from me. I can report exact display digits, light color, wire order and colors at any time. Blind: same drill, act only on my words Mute instructs, go, announce the wire aloud before cutting, then wave for my status report.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏", "👍"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[purple] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ✌ ✊ 🤙]

Mute's line again decodes to a double-encoded go: 👍 received, ✊ ✌ = "cut two," ✊ 🤙 = "cut blue" — and wire 2 is blue. Consistent, no holds. The route for Blind has a wrinkle: raw position counting is no longer mirror-safe (second from one end is blue, second from the other is a cut stub), but intact-wire counting is flip-proof — blue is the middle of the three surviving wires, second intact from either end. And Blind has the twin cut stubs as a superb anchor: blue is the intact wire hugging the stubs on the side toward wire 1. Relaying with all of that plus the standard drills.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Status: no change since my last report, display 9, green light steady, wires purple, blue, cut, cut, white. Now the instruction. Mute instructs: go. Cut wire 2, the blue wire. Blind, here is your route. There are three intact wires left and two cut stubs in the middle of the row. Your target is the middle intact wire, which means it is the second intact wire counting from either end of the row, so this one is flip-proof if you count only intact wires and skip the cut stubs. Second anchor: feel the two cut stubs in the middle. The blue wire is the intact wire directly beside the stubs, on the opposite side from the white wire, between a purple wire and a stub. So: find the stubs, step one wire over away from white, and that is blue. Warning, do not just count raw wires including the stubs, because from one end the second raw wire is blue but from the other end it is a stub. Count intact wires only. Before you cut, say out loud: cutting wire 2, blue. Then cut fully in one motion, wave afterward, and I will report the new state immediately, since the bomb has reshuffled and changed its light after every correct cut so far. Mute: relaying verbatim, Blind announces the step aloud first so you can catch errors. Blind: go now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Third correct cut — and a new pattern emerges: only the end wires survive now, white at position 1 and purple at position 5, with the entire middle of the row severed. Display went 6 → 9 → **7**, so it is not a simple counter; that's a data point for Mute's manual reasoning. Light is now orange. Same drill: exhaustive report, alarm sign to Mute.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Blind: cut three was correct, system confirmed it, hands off until the next go. Everyone, the bomb changed again, full new state. The display has changed again: it now shows 7, so it went 6, then 9, then 7, not a simple counter, Mute, that is yours to interpret. The light is now orange, steady. The wires: wire 1 is white, wires 2, 3 and 4 are all cut, wire 5 is purple. So only two intact wires remain, one at each end of the row: white at the first position, purple at the last position, with a long gap of cut stubs between them. If Blind counts raw positions from either end, the white wire is first and the purple wire is fifth, so each of them has a unique raw position, but Blind should anchor by touch: the white wire is the intact one at one end, the purple is the intact one at the other end. One more fact for the manual, the two intact wires have different textures is something only Blind can confirm, I can only see colors. Mute: send the next instruction in the usual code, with holds if you need more from me, and I can re-report anything on demand. Blind: same drill, act only when you hear me say Mute instructs, go, announce the wire aloud before cutting, wave afterward for my status report.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏", "👍"])
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ☝ ✊ 🤞]

Mute's line: 👍 received, ✊ ☝ = "cut one," ✊ 🤞 = "cut white" — wire 1, the white wire. Consistent, no holds. But before relaying this as a go I have to flag a deadly asymmetry: with only two intact wires left, one at each end, "wire 1" is defined by printed numbers that **Blind cannot feel or read**. From Blind's perspective the row is mirror-symmetric — an intact wire at each end, stubs between. If Blind picks the wrong end, they cut purple instead of white. Every previous cut had a mirror-proof anchor; this one doesn't, and a wrong cut kills us. The fix costs one round and nothing else: Blind touches both end wires and describes every tactile difference aloud (Mute hears Blind directly), Mute maps that to the target or adjusts, and only then do I release the true go. The display has held steady between cuts every time — 6 for seven turns — so there's no evidence of a timer making delay dangerous. I'm deliberately holding Mute's go pending verification, and saying so openly.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Status: no change, display 7, orange light steady, wires white at one end, purple at the other, stubs between. Mute, I received your instruction, cut wire 1, the white wire, and I am putting it on hold for one round, and here is why. Only two intact wires remain, one at each end of the row. The white one is defined by a printed number, and Blind cannot read or feel printed things. From Blind's touch alone the two end wires are mirror images, an intact wire at each end, so Blind cannot yet know which end is position 1. Cutting the wrong end means cutting purple, and we do not get that wrong. So, new drill for this round only. Blind: do not cut yet.
```
